title: Supply of Goods within Agreed Period

content.scenario: A consumer in Delhi orders a smartphone from an online retailer with a promised delivery date of 7 days. However, the retailer delays the delivery by 14 days, causing the consumer to buy the same phone from another retailer at a higher price due to the urgency of the need.
content.outcome: The online retailer's delay in supplying the goods beyond the agreed period, leading to a rise in the price the consumer had to pay elsewhere, constitutes a restrictive trade practice. The consumer may seek redressal for the unjustified costs incurred.

user_queries: What if a retailer delays the delivery of goods?
Can a consumer seek compensation for delay in supply?
Is delaying delivery beyond the agreed time a restrictive trade practice?
